label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L >= 7)
explanation: Delimiter-step unit: about 92% of activation mass falls on the <DEL> step. It fires there for about half of all sequences, mostly long ones: rarely when L <= 5, partly at L = 6, almost always at L >= 8. Magnitude rises with L (to_go = 8 gives the highest rate) and with the first original token, which is also the first token to output: it is stronger when that token is o, a, d, 0, m or w. Weak leftover activity appears on the last original token of 9-long sequences and on the first few copy steps, especially right after the delimiter. It essentially never fires during the first 6 original steps or late in the copy phase, and it does not depend on in_tok outside the delimiter.

issues: The factual claims hold up on dev. 50.1% of <DEL> steps are active and they carry 91.7% of the activation mass. Precision at the <DEL> step by length: L=5 0.06, L=6 0.23, L=7 0.72, L=8 0.98, L=9 0.996. Original steps 0-5 never fire, and late copy steps fire at 1% or less. Last original token at L=9: 17% rate. Copy steps 1-3: weak and sparse (precision 0.03). Test scores reproduce: P 0.897, R 0.692, F1 0.78, mass recall 0.88.

The main systematic false-positive class is L=7 <DEL> steps whose first token is a weak one. Precision with first_tok s is 0.14, h 0.47, v 0.45, j 0.42 and n 0.45, against 0.97-1.0 for a/o/d/0/m/w. The explanation treats the first token only as a magnitude effect, but at L=7 (and even more at L=6) it decides whether the unit crosses threshold at all. The label 'L >= 7' therefore somewhat overclaims L=7.

Fixing this gap barely helps. Gating L=7 and L=6 by first token raises test F1 only from 0.783 to 0.796. Recall is capped because 22.5% of active steps fall outside the <DEL> step (phase==1 alone has recall 0.775), and that leftover activity is diffuse: no copy-step or original-step predicate reaches precision above about 0.4. So no large systematic counterexample class remains, and the agent's stated limitations are accurate.
skeptic.revised_label: <DEL> step of long sequences (always at L >= 8; at L = 7 and L = 6 it depends on the first original token, strongest for o/a/d/0/m/w)
